title: Smooth Reading · Q3 W12 D01
objective: Read grade-level sentences accurately, smoothly, and with meaning.
introduction: Milo is reading a new story aloud! 🐱 Smooth readers say each word correctly, pause at punctuation, and group words into phrases. Ready to explore?

vocabulary.definition: Stop briefly at a punctuation mark when reading aloud.
Say each word correctly while reading.
Read words together in meaningful groups.

items.prompt: Which sentence starts with a capital letter and ends correctly?  (in this lesson: Smooth Reading)
items.explanation: Milo reads. starts with a capital M and ends with a period. 'look out' and 'where is the book' have no end mark, and 'milo reads.' starts with a small letter.

items.prompt: Which choice shows the right capital and end mark?  (in this lesson: Smooth Reading)
items.explanation: 'Where is the book?' starts with a capital W and ends with a question mark. 'where is the book' has no capital letter or end mark, 'look out' has no end mark, and 'milo reads.' starts with a small letter.

items.prompt: Which sentence is written with the correct capital and punctuation?  (in this lesson: Smooth Reading)
items.explanation: 'Look out!' starts with a capital L and ends with an exclamation point. The other choices are missing a capital letter, an end mark, or both.

items.prompt: Which example follows both sentence-mark rules?  (in this lesson: Smooth Reading)
items.explanation: 'We are ready.' starts with a capital W and ends with a period, so it follows both sentence rules. The other choices miss a capital letter or an end mark.

items.prompt: Which sentence starts with a big letter?
items.explanation: Milo reads. starts with a big M. 'milo reads.', 'look out', and 'where is the book' all begin with a small letter.
